_: How the YouK range assembles, as data. Every number here was measured from
the meshes and cross-checked against Kesseboehmer's mounting instructions -
see FINDINGS.md. tools/add-snaps.py turns it into snap planes.
This file is the reviewable artefact. A wrong number here produces a model
that assembles confidently and incorrectly, so it is data in git rather than
_mask: ONE mask per ladder depth, shared by span and hang accessories, because a
rung mount is a rung mount: both families bolt through the same hole in the
same rung face. Giving them separate masks would mean two snaps at the same
point on the frame, and filling one would not fill the other - a shelf and a
tray could then occupy the same rung face. Depth is the axis that actually
gates compatibility, and it is already in the mask.
_rungTops: Height above the frame base of each rung member's TOP face, which is what an
accessory bears down on. Members are 4.9mm thick and start 95.1, 450.1,
805.1 ... above the base. A frame gets every rung whose top fits inside its
height - that rule reproduces the measured rung count on all six frames.
Depth 200 uses a 236.5mm pitch, depth 320 runs 355, 355, 595, 355, 355
between rung centres - the asymmetric-looking 595 is in Kesseboehmer's own
dimension chain and is confirmed in the geometry.
_mountHole: Every rung carries two 5x5mm holes in its top wall, at these distances
either side of the frame's depth centre. Each hang accessory carries a 9x6mm
obround slot over each of them. The two agree on both depths - 320 frames
and 320 accessories both use 95, 200s both use 35 - which is what proves a
hang accessory is centred on the frame's depth rather than offset.
add-snaps.py finds the slot by this number and takes the plug from it, so
the plug is measured from each part rather than typed in per part.
_frames: The ladder frames. Converted with their 320mm depth along X, which cannot be
right - a shelf's width is also along X, and a shelf spans BETWEEN two
frames. rotateYdeg brings the depth onto Z and the 30mm thickness onto X,
the axis the frames are spaced along.
_span: Accessories that span two frames. Each carries a plug at BOTH ends, so the
bay resolves as a chain: frame -> shelf -> frame, with the shelf's width
setting the frame spacing. That is how Kesseboehmer sells it.
The plug sits half a frame thickness in from the part's outer edge, so the
part's end is flush with the frame's outer face. Measured on the 900 shelf:
its end brackets are 29.6mm wide (the frame is 30) centred at x = -460.3,
and half-width minus 15 gives -460.05. Agreement to 0.3mm.
The plug sits at y = 0, the part's base, because the bracket bears down on
the rung's top face - the shelf is dropped in from above per MA 406215.
Verified: the bracket's lowest material lands at exactly 100.0mm, the rung's
top face, with nothing below it.
_hang: Accessories that hang on ONE frame and cantilever off it (MA 406209, MA
406210). They lie across the frame's depth, so like the frames they are
converted with their length along X and want the same 90 degree turn.
All of them share one pressed bracket: a 1.5mm top sheet whose underside
bears on the rung's top face, with the obround slot dropping over the rung's
hole and a leg descending just outside the rung's outer face. add-snaps.py
derives the single plug from that slot, so there is no per-part number to
get wrong - only the id, the depth and the turn.
One plug, not two: nothing attaches to the far side of a hung accessory.
